checked_ok.claim: Cucumber.js 13 is the current major: npm latest 13.2.1 (2026-08-04); 13.0.0 (2026-06-02) added Node 26 support and moved parallel workers to threads; active org-maintained project.

All 11 listed Turkish keywords (Özellik, Geçmiş, Kural, Senaryo, Senaryo taslağı, Örnekler, Diyelim ki, Eğer ki, O zaman, Ve, Fakat) are valid in the official gherkin-languages.json 'tr' entry. Gherkin 39.1.0 (2026-05-06) expanded the Turkish list with many synonyms (e.g. 'Eğer ', 'Durum', 'Vaka'), so restricting to a basic subset is a sound rule.
Cucumber 13.2.1 ships @cucumber/gherkin 42.0.0, which matches the longest step keyword first (JavaScript fix in 32.1.2, 2025-05-25), so 'Eğer ki ...' is not split into 'Eğer ' plus 'ki ...'.
Fastify inject is built in (light-my-request, 6.6.0 on 2026-10-04) and exercises the full app without opening a socket.
4 parallel Cucumber workers is supported: Cucumber 13 runs workers as threads and gives each CUCUMBER_WORKER_ID, CUCUMBER_TOTAL_WORKERS and CUCUMBER_PARALLEL.
4 workers fit a standard GitHub-hosted Linux runner for a public repo (4 CPUs, 16 GB); a private repo runner has 2 CPUs, 8 GB.
Cleaning the database before each scenario instead of wrapping scenarios in a rolled-back transaction matches Cucumber's guidance ('Make sure you clean your database in a Before hook').
Cloning a migrated template with CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE is a supported PostgreSQL pattern; the only rule is that no other session may be connected to the template during the copy.
The Testcontainers PostgreSQL module is current (@testcontainers/postgresql 12.2.0, npm 2026-09-28; core engines node >= 22.22) and also offers snapshot/restoreSnapshot.
'İş kuyruğunun da test saati vardır' is correct: pg-boss 12 (latest 12.36.0) takes a clock option; a TestClock drives polls, cron, backoff and pg-boss's own job_now().
An in-memory mailbox needs no extra package: Nodemailer's stream/JSON transport returns the built message instead of sending it, intended for testing.
Vitest 5 is released and stable: announced 2026-09-03, latest 5.0.3 (npm 2026-09-30); requires Node >= 22.12 and Vite >= 6.4, fine for Node 24/26.
fast-check is current: 4.10.2 (npm 2026-09-19).
A coverage gate limited to the core is supported: Vitest thresholds accept glob keys (e.g. 'packages/core/**') and perFile; @vitest/coverage-v8 5.0.3 matches Vitest 5.
oasdiff is actively released (v1.33.0 on 2026-10-01, several releases in September 2026) and fits as a breaking-change CI gate.
Squawk is actively released (squawk-cli 2.67.0, npm 2026-10-04) and fits as a migration lint gate.
Schemathesis is current and maintained: 4.29.2 released 2026-10-04, Python >= 3.10, MIT (see finding on whether it is worth it now).
Stryker 10.0.0 (2026-08-14) is the current release and supports Node >= 22 (see finding on its Vitest 5 defect).

The Node 24 and 26 CI matrix is compatible with the test stack: Cucumber 13 engines '22 || 24 || >=26', Vitest 5 '^22.12.0 || ^24.0.0 || >=26.0.0', Stryker 10 '>=22.0.0', Testcontainers 12 '>= 22.22'.
k6 can load-test the sync endpoint with realistically signed records: its crypto.subtle supports ECDSA sign (P-256 example), and the current k6 is v2.3.0 (2026-09-21).
k6 scripts can be TypeScript with no build step: k6 transpiles .ts with esbuild by default since v0.57 (types are stripped, not checked).
The example uses the '# language: tr' header and the Given/And/When/Then keywords correctly (Diyelim ki, Ve, Eğer ki, O zaman).

findings.finding: With the plan's own versions (Vitest 5 plus Stryker 10) the mutation gate is broken today. @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner 10.0.0 builds its test-name filter with spaces, but Vitest 5 now matches names joined with ' > ', so zero tests run per covered mutant, every covered mutant is reported Survived and the score collapses (one report: 47.36 to 2.96). The runner's peer range 'vitest >=2.0.0' lets Vitest 5 install cleanly. Issue opened 2026-09-04 is open; fix PR #6214 (2026-09-05) is unmerged; 10.0.0 is still the latest release. Stryker's thresholds.break defaults to null, so CI stays green while the gate protects nothing.

findings.finding: In Cucumber.js, BeforeAll runs once per worker by default, so 'one container, one template, one clone per worker' needs a coordinator-level hook; without it the plan gets 4 containers and 4 migration runs, or a race on the template. The coordinator option (HookTarget.COORDINATOR) only exists since 13.2.0 (2026-07-20), so '13' is not a precise enough floor. PostgreSQL also refuses CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE while any other session is connected to the template, so the migrating connection must be closed first.

evidence.quote: By default, any `BeforeAll` and `AfterAll` hooks you have defined will run _once per worker_.
Add option for where to run global hooks
Coordinator `BeforeAll` hooks run before the workers begin, and coordinator `AfterAll` hooks run after all workers have finished
CREATE DATABASE will fail if any other connection exists when it starts; during the copy operation, new connections to the source database are prevented.

findings.recommendation_tr: Cucumber.js sürümünü 13.2 ve üstü diye yazarım. Her işçi kendi kopyasını CUCUMBER_WORKER_ID ile bulur.

findings.finding: The plan already runs PostgreSQL through Docker Compose for development (line 802) and GitHub Actions has built-in PostgreSQL service containers, so Testcontainers is a second way to start the same database. testcontainers 12.2.0 brings 15 direct dependencies (dockerode, archiver, docker-compose, ssh-remote-port-forward, tar-fs, undici and more). With a fixed database address, the coordinator hook only creates the template and per-worker clones under test-only names, and no container address has to be handed to worker threads. Trade-off: locally 'docker compose up' must be running before tests, and Testcontainers' automatic cleanup is lost.

evidence.quote: "dockerode": "^5.0.1", "archiver": "^7.0.1", "docker-compose": "^1.5.0", "ssh-remote-port-forward": "^1.0.4" (npm view testcontainers@12.2.0 dependencies, 15 entries)

Böylece bir bağımlılık ağacı kalkar ve işçilere adres taşımak gerekmez. Bedeli: yerelde testten önce docker compose up açık olmalı; veritabanına ulaşılamazsa test açık bir mesajla durur. findings.finding: Emptying tables does not reset state held in memory. @fastify/rate-limit and Better Auth keep rate-limit counters in memory by default, and every inject request comes from 127.0.0.1, so in a worker that reuses one app instance the counters of earlier scenarios leak into later ones (random 429 responses). Better Auth's limiter is also off outside production by default, so the plan's tight limit on code endpoints is not exercised unless the test config turns it on. An app left open also keeps pool and job-queue connections that TRUNCATE (ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock) has to wait for.

evidence.quote: by default, this plugin uses an in-memory store.
an optional string specifying the client remote address. Defaults to '127.0.0.1'.
Rate limiting is disabled in development mode by default.
At the end of your tests it is highly recommended to call `.close()` to ensure that all connections to external services get closed.

findings.finding: pg-boss tables are part of the migrated schema (line 592). pg-boss reads its schema version from its own 'version' table and keeps queue definitions and schedules in tables. A blanket TRUNCATE of every table empties that bookkeeping; skipping the pgboss schema leaves a deferred job from one scenario to fire in the next when the test clock advances. The plan does not say which tables are emptied.

findings.finding: The fake clock reaches only code that asks the clock interface. pg-boss's TestClock covers pg-boss's own statements but, per its docs, does not change PostgreSQL now() or application SQL. Better Auth computes the e-mail code expiry with Date.now(), so the 5-minute code rule cannot be moved by the core's fake clock. Any rule time taken from SQL now() or the system clock will disagree with the fake clock in scenarios (arrival time, 7-day send deadline, term lock).

evidence.quote: it does not change pg_catalog.now() or your own SQL
Pass a `TestClock` to drive time by hand in tests; it also takes over the Postgres side, so `${schema}.job_now()` reports the same time for pg-boss's own statements.
return new Date(Date.now() + (unit === "sec" ? span * 1000 : span));

findings.finding: Two problems. (1) Line 407 defines the allowance as an integer formula, so 'compared with the integer calculation' reads as the formula compared with itself, a test that cannot go red; the oracle must be the rule's definition (the largest k with (T-k)*100 >= p*T, found by counting). (2) fast-check samples at random with a default of 100 runs, so 'thousands of inputs' needs an explicit numRuns and still never means 'every T'. T is a small bounded integer and p has two values, so a plain loop over T = 0..1000 for p = 70 and 80 checks every case deterministically in milliseconds with no extra tool. fast-check fits the multi-input rules (clock drift allowance, window edges, flags).

findings.finding: The reset strategy writes on every scenario (TRUNCATE of all data tables, with commit) and on every run (template clone). A test database needs no crash safety; PostgreSQL documents turning off fsync, synchronous_commit and full_page_writes, or using a RAM disk, to run much faster. This is a few server flags, no new tool.

evidence.quote: durability adds significant database overhead, so if your site does not require such a guarantee, PostgreSQL can be configured to run much faster.

findings.recommendation_tr: Test veritabanını dayanıklılık ayarları kapalı çalıştırırım: fsync, synchronous_commit ve full_page_writes kapalı, CI'da veri klasörü bellekte. Bu yalnız test ve geliştirme kabı için; yayın veritabanında asla.

compactness_notes: Two runners vs one: keep Cucumber.js 13 for server behaviour and Vitest 5 for the core. The one-runner options fail the sustainability lens. QuickPickle (Vitest plugin) has 52 GitHub stars, one npm maintainer, last release 1.11.2 on 2026-05-06, pins @cucumber/gherkin ^32 while upstream is 42, and pulls pngjs, lodash and image tools for visual testing. @amiceli/vitest-cucumber has 101 stars, one maintainer, its own parser instead of the official Gherkin one, depends on ts-morph, writes steps per scenario inside describeFeature (poor reuse of Turkish steps), and its Turkish support is not confirmed. Cucumber.js is org-maintained (5.4k stars, Open Collective, OpenSSF scorecard, four releases June to August 2026) and ships the official parser with the May 2026 Turkish keyword list. The two runners test different packages (core vs server), so their configs do not overlap, and .feature files stay portable if this is revisited. Leanest gate set that still guards the allowance formula, the time rules and the sync endpoint: per change: Biome, type check, contract regeneration diff, oasdiff, drizzle-kit check, Squawk, Vitest (core coverage >= 90%, exhaustive allowance table against the counting definition, fast-check for clock and flag rules, model test of the phone send queue), Cucumber with 4 workers (plus a fast-check model test of the sync endpoint through inject). Weekly, one scheduled job instead of nightly plus weekly: Stryker on packages/core (command runner until stryker-js PR #6214 ships, with thresholds.break) and a k6 --once smoke run. Before release: k6 peak test with an arrival-rate executor on a production-size server. Later: Schemathesis. Net moving parts: minus Schemathesis and the Python toolchain in CI, minus testcontainers and @testcontainers/postgresql (if F05 is accepted), minus @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner while it is broken, tsx not added if native type stripping works; nothing added (fast-check, k6, Vitest and the GitHub service container are already in the stack or built in). Line 540 (Teknolojiler özeti) must be updated with whatever is removed.
open_questions: Is the repository public or private? Public GitHub runners have 4 CPUs (matches '4 paralel koşu'); private ones have 2 CPUs and consume the account's CI minutes, which also affects nightly versus weekly jobs.
When will stryker-js PR #6214 (Vitest 5 test name separator) be released? Once it ships, the faster per-test Vitest runner can replace the command runner.
Does Cucumber 13 load .ts step files through Node 24's native type stripping inside its worker threads in a pnpm workspace without tsx? Cucumber's docs only document tsx; needs a skeleton check.
With pg-boss tables created by migration files (migrate off), does emptying only the job table between scenarios leave pg-boss fully working under TestClock? Needs a skeleton check.
Does Cucumber 13.2 create worker threads after coordinator BeforeAll hooks finish, so that environment values set there reach workers? Only matters if Testcontainers stays (random port).
